value_types.bool: true or false. Test with operator 'is' and value true or false.
value_types.length: A length; values may carry a unit (pt, mm, cm, in). Without a unit the check's unit parameter applies.
value_types.percent: A percentage 0-100 (ink amounts may exceed 100 for totals).
value_types.resolution: Pixels per inch; values may be written as 300 or '300ppi'.
value_types.bytes: A size in the unit given by the check's unit parameter.
value_types.version: A PDF version such as 1.7 or 2.0, compared numerically.
value_types.enum: One of the values listed in the check's notes.
value_types.list: A set of values. 'includes' and 'excludes' test membership; 'count' compares the number of entries.
value_types.size: Width and height given in the check's parameters; compared in either orientation if allowed.

operators.==: Equal. Text is compared exactly, numbers within the atom's tolerance.
operators.multiple_of: The number is a whole multiple of the value (within the tolerance).
operators.is: Boolean test: the check's answer is the given true/false value. A false test matches exactly the objects for which the property is false.
operators.in: The value equals one entry of the given list.
operators.not_in: The value equals no entry of the given list.
operators.contains: The value contains the given text.
operators.starts_with: The value starts with the given text.
operators.ends_with: The value ends with the given text.
operators.matches: The whole value matches the regular expression.
operators.finds: The regular expression matches somewhere in the value.
operators.occurs_in: The value appears inside the given text.
operators.includes: The list contains the given entry (or all given entries).
operators.excludes: The list contains none of the given entries.
operators.count: Compare the number of list entries; combine with a comparison: {"op": "count", "compare": ">", "value": 2}.
operators.fits_within: The measured size is not larger than the given size in either dimension.
operators.exceeds: The measured size is larger than the given size in at least one dimension.

atom options.case_sensitive: false makes text operators ignore case (default true).
atom options.tolerance: Numeric tolerance in the value's unit.

checks.title: Enough contrast against the background
checks.description: Contrast between the colour of text or a graphic and the rendered colour right behind it meets the minimum for its kind.

params.name: kind
params.default_reason: Text contrast is the requirement most documents are measured against.

params.name: normal_text_ratio
params.default_reason: WCAG 2.2 1.4.3 minimum for normal text.

params.name: large_text_ratio
params.default_reason: WCAG 2.2 1.4.3 minimum for large text.

params.name: graphics_ratio
params.default_reason: WCAG 2.2 1.4.11 minimum for graphics.

params.name: large_size
params.default_reason: WCAG treats 18pt text as large.

params.name: large_bold_size
params.default_reason: WCAG treats 14pt bold text as large.

params.name: resolution
params.default_reason: Enough to find the background colour; text shapes need not be resolved.

checks.notes: The page is rendered once; the background is the most frequent colour in the text box (for text) or in a thin ring around the shape (for graphics) that differs from the object's own colour. Colours, including CMYK and spot colours, are turned into relative luminance through the colour engine. Invisible text, whitespace, artifacts, hidden layers, shadings, page-sized shapes and shapes that cannot be seen at all (contrast below 1.05) are skipped. Bold means a bold font name, weight 600 or more, or the ForceBold flag.

top_level.name: Display name.

check.name: Unique name; shown in reports and used by only_where, objects and plan steps.
check.all: Conditions that must all hold for the same object.

condition.check: A catalogue id such as page.box_size.
condition.<parameter>: Named parameters of the catalogue check, e.g. "box": "trim".
condition.objects: Names of other checks whose objects this condition compares against (content.relation).

check.scope: page (default), trim or bleed: limits object checks to content inside that box.

report_when.document_hits: Report only when the number of hits in the document satisfies this comparison, e.g. "> 3".

check.max_hits_per_page: Stop counting after this many hits on one page.
check.silent: Evaluate but do not report; used by only_where and objects.

fix.fix: A catalogue fix id such as page.set_box.
fix.only_where: Check names; the fix runs only on pages where one of them hit.

variables.name: Identifier used as {name}.
variables.label: Prompt text.
variables.script: JavaScript computing the value; it can read kura.document, kura.variables and kura.results.
variables.override: Values are supplied with --var name=value (CLI) or the vars field (API).

convert.level: Target standard, e.g. pdfa-2b or pdfx-4.
convert.also: Second standard written into the same file (PDF/A + PDF/X).
convert.reconvert: Convert once more from the first result when it is not yet compliant.

raster_fallback.resolution: Pixels per inch for pages turned into images when conversion fails (default 300ppi).
raster_fallback.keep_text: Keep the text invisible on top (default true).

step.do: check, fix, profile, variable or revert.
step.fix: For do=fix: a fix name or inline fix.
step.profile: For do=profile: path of another Kura profile.

next.pass: Step id after a clean result.

plan.results: Each step's result is available to later scripts as kura.results[i] with hits and pages.

script_api.kura.variable(name, default): Read a variable, setting the default when empty.
script_api.kura.document: {name, pageCount, pages: [{number, mediaBox, cropBox, bleedBox, trimBox, artBox, userUnit}]} (boxes as {left, bottom, right, top}).
script_api.kura.results: Results of earlier plan steps: [{step, hits, pages}].
script_api.limits: 5 s run time, 64 MB memory, no file or network access.

stamp_api.window.kura.pages: [{number, mediaBox, trimBox, bleedBox, cropBox, artBox, rotation}] in points.
stamp_api.kura.onPages(callback): Register a function called once per page; inside it update the DOM and call kura.printPages(1).
stamp_api.kura.printPages(count): Emit the current DOM as the stamp for the next count pages.
stamp_api.barcodes: <object type="application/barcode"> with param type and data renders a barcode.

output_codes.CHECK_NOT_EVALUATED: A condition could not be evaluated for this file.
output_codes.PROFILE_INVALID: The profile is not valid Kura JSON; the message names the field.
output_codes.PROFILE_EMPTY: The profile has no checks to run in check mode.
output_codes.PROFILE_TARGET: The profile's convert section chose the target standard.
output_codes.FIX_SCHEDULED: A fix will run during conversion.
output_codes.FIX_NOT_NEEDED: A fix's only_where checks found nothing.
output_codes.FIX_UNKNOWN: The fix id is not in the catalogue.
output_codes.ICC_PROFILE_MISSING: A named ICC profile was not found.
output_codes.PLAN_STEP: A plan step ran; the message gives its result and the next step.
output_codes.PLAN_NO_CONVERSION: The plan ran no converting step; output equals input.
output_codes.hit_message: '<severity>: <check name> (<n> hit(s), pages <ranges>)' with the check's description when given.
